1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 7.5% and holds for 15 samples as the bushing diagnosis lands (*2,055 viewers regained, 49.0% present, 81st percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“I just got tank slappers again” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind to catch the callback and verdict: "we thought it was just the neck bolts... I just got tank slappers again." 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 3-second on-screen recap card of the Ep 02 neck-bolt fix at 5:15 so first-time viewers get the callback the rewinders wanted. 5 · rationaleA reveal earning rewinds is an asset; making the setup legible on first watch converts the replay into forward retention.
peak8:09
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 5.8% but holds only 3 samples as the dealership arrival lands (*1,656 viewers regained, 50.2% present, 77th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“Fingers crossed they can help me out” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind to the handoff moment: "That's so cool. Fast wheels cranky" and the size-large bars appearing. 4 · how (the next move)Tease the size-large bars at 7:57 with a riser under "Fingers crossed they can help me out" so anticipation carries into the reveal. 5 · rationaleRisers ~20 seconds before a key moment flatten retention through the buildup and hold more of the room to the payoff.

They rattle." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 8:46-9:30 of dealership chatter and rejoin on the size-large bars going on so the sequence ends on visible progress, not thanks. 5 · rationalePositive progression holds; stripping-down and thank-you beats after the answer lands are where pace collapses in a repair sequence.

peak21:39

1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime26:55 gone by 0:3022.8% at halfway34% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:15
1 · what the curve showedAudience slides from 100% to 77.2% across the first 17 seconds, but this is milder than the channel's usual open (*3.8x local, 4,871 viewers, +13.2pp above channel median at 0:30*). 2 · evidence at that second“we're going to give her a good wash” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Standard channel greeting and premise setup — 'we're going to give her a good wash today cuz she is filthy' — before any stake is named. 4 · how (the next move)Hold the current cold-open; do not surgery an intro that already beats 269 of 299 sibling videos at 0:30. 5 · rationalePackaging and open agree here — the intro loss sits below the channel's 13.4% average for intros, so cutting risks a working asset.
peak9:58
1 · what the curve showedA second replay cluster pulls 585 viewers back and holds them for two samples at the 74th percentile (*5.1% rise, 40.3% present*). 2 · evidence at that second“Jordan's going to come try to help me” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Same lift beat, one sample earlier — 'Jordan's going to come try to help me... get that down' — viewers are scrubbing to catch the setup before the payoff. 4 · how (the next move)Keep the lift setup and payoff contiguous; do not intercut b-roll between 9:47 and 10:03 in the edit. 5 · rationaleTwo adjacent rewind peaks on the same beat mean viewers want the full micro-arc uninterrupted — Hayden's known-destination, unknown-route loop.
drop10:14
1 · what the curve showedStop rate hits 2.1x the channel norm and 1,259 viewers leave in 32 seconds, on a moment that also drew rewinds (*9.8x local, 42.9%→38.1%*). 2 · evidence at that second“one two two three there that was so much easier” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Jordan takes over the physical task — 'one two two three there that was so much easier' — resolving the 'can she lift it alone' tension the segment was built on. 4 · how (the next move)Trim 10:21-10:38 (the post-lift chatter about aluminum poles) and cut straight from the successful lift into her solo re-attempt. 5 · rationaleTension spent means audience leaves — Joos: retention drops the instant conflict resolves, so shorten the gap between resolution and the next question.
peak10:14
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 6.4% and 773 viewers scrub back, landing in the 75th percentile against similar videos (*42.9% present, held one sample*). 2 · evidence at that second“that was so much easier” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The successful two-person lift — 'that was so much easier... it's just the weight' — is the moment that proves the video's title premise about the bike being too big. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this lift attempt into the first two minutes as a cold-open tease, then return to it in place at 10:00. 5 · rationaleJoos peak-end rule: the moment viewers rewind to is the video's thesis proof — surfacing it early makes the packaging promise land inside the first minute.
drop14:16
1 · what the curve showedA 65-second stretch bleeds 1,169 viewers at twice the channel's normal stop rate and sits in the 37th percentile against peers (*9.4x local, 36.0%→31.8%*). 2 · evidence at that second“husband washes my bike for me” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The segment is a wordless music-and-applause montage of the husband washing the bike — no dialogue, no progression, just '[Music]... [Applause]... [Music]'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 14:16-15:21 to under 20 seconds, keep one visual gag from the wash, and voice-over what she is thinking while watching. 5 · rationaleJoos: pacing is flow of NEW information every ~5 seconds — a silent montage delivers none, and this is the video's single worst-performing stretch.
peak24:46
1 · what the curve showedLate in the video 319 viewers scrub back and stay up for eight samples, unusual this deep into the runtime (*5.0% rise, 22.4% present, 69th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“if you guys want to go cck walking” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A direct call-to-action for a new format — 'if you guys want to go cck walking and fishing with me... let me know leave a comment' — viewers rewinding to hear the offer. 4 · how (the next move)Test a dedicated creek-walking video within the next upload cycle; success signal is comment volume above her recent motorcycle uploads. 5 · rationaleA held rewind at 92% through the video is a demand signal — Trahan: high retention on a beat is evidence the audience will follow it into its own video. cautionShe notes the old creek videos 'didn't really perform well' — verify whether the packaging or the content underperformed before rebuilding the format.

1 · what the curve showedA 30-second stretch mid-video loses 2,635 viewers at 3.1x the channel's normal stop rate here (*7.4x the surrounding rate, 3.44% vs 1.10% channel-typical*). 2 · evidence at that second“don't trust the forecast” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The bear-box tip resolves, then a soft segue restates the next tip twice before delivering it — 'don't be irresponsible with food do not trust the forecast'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 8:28-8:43 and jump straight from the bear-box wrap to 'use your own judgment on the forecast', dropping the double 'don't trust the forecast' setup. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information — repeating the forecast headline before delivering it is exactly the verbal repetition that flattens a mid-video segue into a valley.
peak9:55

drop14:12
1 · what the curve showedThe audience senses the ending here and 2,561 leave in 30 seconds, dropping to 16.0% (*4.6x the channel's normal stop rate, 20th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“so those are my helpful tips” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The wrap-signal lands explicitly — 'so those are my helpful tips' — then rolls into gear-shopping plans, a comment ask, a playlist plug and 'quick and easy video'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 14:02-14:36 down to a single sentence and end on the strongest unused tip held in reserve, then hand straight to the end screen within 10 seconds. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment viewers sense the outro — signalling 'those are my tips' then stacking plugs is why this trails 20% of comparable videos here.

drop0:18

Critical failure comparing the DJI Action 5 Pro vs. GoPro 13 Action Camera

published 2024-10-14 · analysed 2026-08-26

1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime11:58 gone by 0:3039.4% at halfway28% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:06
1 · what the curve showedThe first eight seconds shed audience to 84.8%, 7.7pp below the channel's median and worse than all 29 other videos at 0:15 (*6,347 viewers, 2.5x spike*). 2 · evidence at that second“let's see which one is best for you” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The open is a spec announcement and a passive framing question: "let's see which one is best for you" before any stake or motorcycling context. 4 · how (the next move)Rebuild the first 8 seconds the way "What Happened To Me?" opens, leading with the GoPro shutting off mid-ride from the 3:13 clip. 5 · rationaleThe channel's best intro holds 100%; opening on the failure delivers the title's promise instantly instead of restating the thumbnail.
drop1:19
1 · what the curve showedA seven-second music sting drops the room from 49.0% to 45.3%, running 2.1x the channel's norm here (*1,665 viewers, 2.8x spike*). 2 · evidence at that second“let me know which one you think is better” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The criteria list ends and hands off to a silent music bumper: "let me know which one is better" then [Music], with no next beat teed up. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 1:22-1:26 of music and hard-cut from "which one is better" straight into the 3:13 GoPro shutoff as the first test. 5 · rationalePacing is flow of new information; a music bumper after a list is repetition, and dropping it lets conflict start while anticipation is live.
drop3:28
1 · what the curve showedThe audio A/B walkthrough loses 878 viewers across 14 seconds at 4.5x the surrounding stop rate, though only 1.2x the channel's norm here (*35.6% remaining*). 2 · evidence at that second“exact same audio exact same settings” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The moment restates the setup instead of playing the comparison: "exact same audio exact same settings I don't have any wind noise deflection on." 4 · how (the next move)Cut 3:22-3:35 and jump straight from the GoPro reboot into the raw side-by-side audio, captioning "DJI" and "GoPro" on screen. 5 · rationaleRetention editing says fast cuts until conflict, none during it; the settings recap delays the actual audio the viewer clicked to hear.
peak11:22
1 · what the curve showedThe room rises 4.2% and holds four samples at 21.3%, 65th percentile versus similar videos (*599 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“hopefully it didn't shut off again” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind the on-camera moment of the GoPro appearing to survive the ride: "hopefully it didn't shut off again oh okay no." 4 · how (the next move)Cut to a tight insert of the GoPro screen at 11:22 and hold the "oh okay no" beat two seconds longer before the verdict. 5 · rationaleStretching a conflict beat with bare sound holds retention; the rewinds show this micro-payoff is doing narrative work already.
peak11:29
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs 5.5% and holds three samples at 22.4%, sitting at the 67th percentile versus similar videos (*825 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“longer battery life quicker recording time” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind the verdict being read out: "DJI has a longer battery life quicker recording time and obviously more reliability." 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this exact verdict as a 10-second cold open before 0:06, then let the video prove each of the three claims in order. 5 · rationaleThe reveal that earns rewinds is an asset; teasing it up top delivers the title promise and structures the middle around three checkable claims.
peak11:36
1 · what the curve showedA one-sample bump lifts the room 3.3% to 23.2% at the 67th percentile, the video's end-point (*529 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“$50 cheaper than the GoPro” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind the price line closing the verdict: "osmo action 5 coming in at $50 cheaper than the GoPro." 4 · how (the next move)Overlay the "$50 cheaper" price on screen at 11:36 and cut the following 15 seconds of thanks and description plug. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment viewers sense the outro; ending on the price hit preserves the emotional high the rewinds already mark.

drop0:12
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 14 seconds shed about a fifth of the room, but slightly less than this channel usually loses here (*9.16% stop rate vs 10.25% typical, 3,939 viewers, 0.9x channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“welcome to the mototi experience I am” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Standard channel-greeting open: 'welcome to the mototi experience I am out here in Tennessee' before the Dragon promise lands at 0:11. 4 · how (the next move)Trial opening on the 0:11 line 'guess where they took me tail of the freaking Dragon' and push the greeting to after the first riding shot. 5 · rationaleThis intro loss (16.2%) already runs above the channel's own intro average (13.4%), so front-loading the title promise attacks the one segment underperforming its cohort.
drop5:36

I've been doing a lot of Tours this year'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 5:08-5:34 (t-shirt and itinerary) and 5:52-6:05 (channel meta), rejoining on the 5:44 'gaggle of goose' riding line over Smoky Mountain b-roll. 5 · rationaleThe signal 'tail of the dragon's done' releases the titular promise mid-video with runtime left, exactly when Joos warns tension must stay live.

peak20:16

drop0:11

peak10:49

drop11:13

peak17:01

drop17:13

drop0:18
1 · what the curve showedThe audience collapses from 95.8% to 65.9% in eighteen seconds right as the narrator finishes selling the trip (*7.5x surrounding stop rate, 22,492 viewers, 1.3x channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“booked our flights packed our bags” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The narrator restates the thumbnail premise then announces logistics instead of showing the Alps: "booked our flights packed our bags". 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:15-0:24 and open on the first riding shot from the peak at 14:56, then drop the "born and raised in Ohio" narration back in over b-roll. 5 · rationaleThe intro is selling the premise the thumbnail already sold, and the Joos rule says never restate what packaging promised — open on the strongest riding moment instead.
peak3:03
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 6.2% for a single sample as the riders enter the Euro tunnel (*2,252 viewers regained, 64th percentile, held one sample*). 2 · evidence at that second“get ready everybody this is what” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)First on-camera conflict beat with genuine anticipation: "get ready everybody this is what it's going to be" over the tunnel entry. 4 · how (the next move)Extend this beat to five seconds by holding the tunnel entry shot with sound-only, and trim the "can't cuss children watch" aside that follows. 5 · rationaleJoos: stretching a conflict beat with bare sound can triple its screen time with stable retention — a one-sample tick suggests the beat is being cut away from too fast. cautionSingle-sample peaks can be data artifacts on a 30-minute video; A/B the extended cut and keep it only if the sample widens.
peak10:03
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 9.4% as the narrator transitions from highway to the Vosges mountain roads (*2,599 viewers regained, held five samples, 68th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“afternoon brought us to the voge mountains” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The line "the afternoon brought us to the voge mountains" delivers a concrete location change and names the payoff — "sweeping bends and hair pins was pure joy". 4 · how (the next move)Add a 20-second riser under 9:56-10:15 and hold the first hair-pin shot on-screen for a full beat before cutting away. 5 · rationaleJoos: risers ~20 seconds before a key moment can hold up to 10% more of the room to the payoff, and this is a proven interest beat to protect.
peak14:56
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 12.3% and holds for twelve samples as the narrator introduces Grimsel Pass (*3,535 viewers regained, 83rd percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“grimsel p Pass riding up the 7,000 ft” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The narrator names the specific reward and stacks superlatives: "grimsel p Pass riding up the 7,000 ft was breathtaking" with "views fell CGI". 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 6-second cut of the Grimsel hair pins into the first 30 seconds as the cold open, replacing the "born and raised in Ohio" voice-over. 5 · rationaleThe strongest replay in the video is a named-reward reveal — Joos says a reveal that earns rewinds should be teased early and structured toward.
drop17:59
1 · what the curve showedA 55-second music-only stretch loses viewers at 1.3x the channel's rate for this position (*6.6x surrounding stop rate, 1,865 viewers, stop rate 1.61% vs 1.22% typical*). 2 · evidence at that second“about to start the most famous part” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Four consecutive music tags with no narration or new information before the narrator finally re-enters at 18:23 with "we are about to start the most famous part of grimsel pass". 4 · how (the next move)Cut 17:37-18:17 down to a single 10-second music beat and move the "most famous part of grimsel pass" line to 17:40 so the tease lands before viewers disengage. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information every ~5 seconds; forty seconds of pure music with no progression is exactly the repetition Joos says to kill.
drop28:57
1 · what the curve showedA 37-second block drops the audience from 27.8% to 25.5% at 3.2x the channel norm for this position (*7.0x surrounding stop rate, 1,626 viewers, stop rate 4.10% vs 1.29% typical*). 2 · evidence at that second“well that was scary” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The narrator releases tension with "well that was scary" then pivots into a Stelvio Pass teaser — viewers sense the payoff has landed and the video is wrapping. 4 · how (the next move)Cut the "well that was scary" beat and the Stelvio voice-over at 28:53-29:08; end on the riding sound from 28:36 and hand straight to the Part 2 end screen. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment viewers sense the ending — never signal the outro, and never resolve tension with runtime left; break off at the emotional high. cautionVerify the Stelvio line is not the load-bearing hook for Part 2; if it is, move it to the end-screen card instead of cutting outright.

drop12:05

peak12:05

drop0:11

drop2:35

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:17
1 · what the curve showedThe opening bleeds from 98.2% to 80.5% across seventeen seconds (*10.0x spike, 5,719 viewers lost*), but the 0:30 hold still beats 296 of 299 channel videos. 2 · evidence at that second“in July of 2015 a 26-year-old newlywed” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A third-person narrator sets up backstory before the rider appears: "in July of 2015 a 26-year-old newlywed" opens with exposition rather than stakes. 4 · how (the next move)Trial opening on the Honda call itself ("receives an exciting call from Honda") and fold the 2015 backstory in later once the trip is in motion. 5 · rationaleThe intro already outperforms channel median by 16.3pp at 0:30, so protect that lead by front-loading the call that made the trip happen. cautionVerify the 2015 setup isn't needed to sell later emotional beats; if it is, keep a two-sentence version and only cut the newlywed framing.
peak16:09
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs 1.3% to 28.2% and holds for five samples (*129 viewers regained*), the longest-held rewind in the video at the 54th percentile. 2 · evidence at that second“comparison is the thief of Joy” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Rewind lands on the reframe line — "comparison is the thief of Joy" — the aphorism viewers scrub back to catch and quote. 4 · how (the next move)Isolate this line with a two-second silence and on-screen text so first-time viewers register it without needing to rewind. 5 · rationaleTwo consecutive replay peaks inside twenty seconds prove this confession sequence is the video's emotional core — signpost it instead of hiding it in narration.
peak16:26
1 · what the curve showedThe audience rises 1.8% to 28.7% and holds for four samples (*180 viewers regained*), sitting at the 56th percentile against similar videos. 2 · evidence at that second“constantly playing ketchup” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind into the emotional confession that just landed: "I did feel like an outsider constantly playing ketchup" — the vulnerability beat behind the montage. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this confession earlier in the trip sequence and cap the wordless music that follows at ten seconds so the payoff isn't buried. 5 · rationaleA replay peak on a spoken confession followed by a flagged drop in the same music bed means the words are the asset — the montage is the tax.
drop16:43
1 · what the curve showedA 68-second stretch loses 796 viewers at (*14.0x the surrounding stop rate, 2.3x the channel norm here*), pulling the audience from 28.9% to 27.5%. 2 · evidence at that second“[16:19] [Music] [16:27] [Music]” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The transcript is three music cues back-to-back — "[16:19] [Music] [16:27] [Music] [16:42] [Music]" — a wordless montage with no new information arriving. 4 · how (the next move)Cut the montage to under 20 seconds and cross-cut it with the next spoken beat so something changes on screen every five seconds. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information; a minute-plus of music with no narration reads as static and stops 2.3x more viewers than the channel norm.
peak22:06

1 · what the curve showedThe 8:40-8:51 stretch loses 211 viewers at 1.3x the channel norm on a music-only gap with no dialogue (*11.7x the preceding stop rate, 34.2% down to 33.0%*). 2 · evidence at that second“is that a couch” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A 14-second silent music beat sits between an ergonomics complaint and a throwaway "is that a couch" — nothing new is introduced, verbal or visual, that the transcript records. 4 · how (the next move)Cut the 8:40-8:54 music gap and land directly on the couch spot, or overlay a tease of the upcoming trip reveal that the intro withheld. 5 · rationaleSomething should visibly change every ~5 seconds (Joos); a 14-second dead beat at the video's midpoint is exactly the valley a pattern interrupt should fill. cautionThe gap may cover a genuine visual moment the transcript cannot see; if b-roll carries the beat, shorten rather than delete and re-check retention.
peak11:21
1 · what the curve showedA smaller replay bump 12 seconds before the main peak, holding for 12 samples on the lead-in to the confession (*96 viewers regained, 1.7% rise, 31.4% present, 60th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“I didn't get as wet this time” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers are scrubbing back to catch the setup — "I didn't get as wet this time I think I was just going too fast" — that precedes the anxiety admission. 4 · how (the next move)Preserve the 11:21-11:33 runway intact when editing; do not tighten the water-crossing callback that primes the confession. 5 · rationaleThe pair of peaks shows viewers treat this as one continuous moment; cutting the setup would flatten the payoff the audience is actively rewinding for.
peak11:33
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 6.3% and holds for 11 samples as she opens up about riding anxiety (*372 viewers regained, 33.4% present, 61st percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“I really struggle with anxiety in my head” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)This is the emotional core the title promised — "I really struggle with anxiety in my head" — landing as a genuine confession after 11 minutes of ride footage. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 10-second cut of this confession into the first 45 seconds as the real stake, then let the ride footage pay it off. 5 · rationaleThe intro currently teases a trip; the audience is actually rewinding for the vulnerability. Leading with the WHY (Hayden) matches what the curve says viewers want. cautionMoving the confession forward may weaken its landing here; A/B a shortened tease up front while keeping the full beat at 11:33, and watch whether 0:30 retention rises without the peak collapsing.

I'm the Queen of Dumb Decisions... Expensive Lessons

published 2024-03-04 · analysed 2026-08-26

1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime25:47 gone by 0:3023.1% at halfway32% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

drop0:14
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 16 seconds behave exactly like this channel's typical intro, shedding roughly a quarter of the room (*4.2x spike, 8,171 viewers, 100.0% to 76.9%*). 2 · evidence at that second“waiting for my friend Missy” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The open is a soft greeting and a wait — 'good morning and welcome' followed by 'I'm actually waiting for my friend Missy' before any stakes land. 4 · how (the next move)Trial re-cutting the first 15 seconds to open cold on a riding-day payoff moment already in the footage, with the greeting deleted entirely. 5 · rationaleThe intro segment lost 0.0% versus the channel's 13.4% average for intros, so the segment itself is fine — but Joos's rule bans channel greetings at frame one, and by 0:30 this video is already 13.5pp above channel median, proving the room rewards a stronger open. cautionVerify the greeting is not a series convention viewers return for; if it is, keep a one-second version and A/B against a cold open on views-per-hour.
drop5:40
1 · what the curve showedA quiet confession beat loses 1.5x the channel's usual rate here (*5.3x local spike, 927 viewers, 38.6% to 36.2%*). 2 · evidence at that second“not been anywhere near what I imagined” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The host breaks tone to admit the trip is failing — 'this snowb biring thing has not been anywhere near what I imagined' — with no visual change to carry it. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 5:32-5:56 down to the single sentence about the trip disappointing, and cross-cut it with B-roll of the cramped camper or Jordan working on the Sportster. 5 · rationaleJoos: pacing is flow of new information, and something should visibly change every ~5 seconds; a static talking-head admission with no image movement is exactly the sag pattern, and this moment runs 1.5x the channel's own norm.
peak8:00
1 · what the curve showedViewers rewind into the arrival at Salt Shack, adding 3.2% of the room over three samples (*509 viewers regained, 52nd percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“right on the lake” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A location reveal lands right after the emotional beat — 'we just got to this little place called salt Shack… we are actually right on the lake' — a change of scene the room wanted to see. 4 · how (the next move)Move the Salt Shack arrival shot 20 seconds earlier and start anticipatory music under the preceding confession so the location lands as release. 5 · rationaleJoos: start risers ~20 seconds before a key moment to flatten retention through the buildup; the confession at 5:40 is losing 1.5x norm precisely because nothing signals a scene change is coming.
peak10:03
1 · what the curve showedThe audience scrubs back to the shopping reveal, adding 5% of the room and holding for three samples (*792 viewers regained, 65th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“probably the nicest reare shocks” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The husband lists what he bought — 'probably the nicest reare shocks… some foxes some handlebars… and some future project upgrades' — a concrete parts reveal viewers rewind to catch. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 3-second tease of the bought parts inside the first minute, with an on-screen 'what did we buy' question that resolves at 10:03. 5 · rationaleJoos: dopamine spikes at the announcement of a reward, not the reward — a tease at 0:30 exploits the already channel-best opening (95.4% held) to pull the room toward the moment they're rewinding for anyway.
peak17:01
1 · what the curve showedThe audience returns to the roadside pull-over anecdote, adding 2.2% over four samples (*307 viewers regained, 46th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“pulled off on the side of the road pass six cars” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The host describes cutting past stopped traffic — 'I just pulled off on the side of the road pass six cars and turned' — a self-deprecating driving admission that lands on the video's 'dumb decisions' promise. 4 · how (the next move)Tease this line inside the first 60 seconds as a cold cut — audio only over a shot of stopped traffic — and let it pay off at 17:01 unchanged. 5 · rationalePackaging promises 'dumb decisions' and this is the clearest in-video example; Joos's rule that packaging makes promises the video must keep argues for surfacing it early, since the channel-best 0:30 hold proves the room will wait.
drop17:32
1 · what the curve showedA 46-second bike-parts exchange between the host and a friend loses fewer viewers than the channel usually loses here (*14.0x local spike, 708 viewers, 0.3x the channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“Fox suspension right yep what are they 13s” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Two riders trade suspension specs — 'Fox suspension right… what are they 13s yep' — insider talk with no stakes for a general viewer, but this channel's audience tolerates it. 4 · how (the next move)Keep the segment; tighten 17:20-17:45 by dropping the repeated '13s' confirmation and the passenger-peg aside so the beat lands in roughly 25 seconds. 5 · rationaleThe moment runs at 0.3x channel norm and is flagged typical for this channel, so surgery is unwarranted — but Joos's kill-all-repetition rule still licenses trimming the duplicated confirmations.

1 · what the curve showedA 36-second music-only stretch mid-video loses 880 viewers, though the stop rate matches channel norm (*3.4x the surrounding stop rate, 0.9x vs channel*). 2 · evidence at that second“[Music] he [Music]” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The transcript is pure music cues with no spoken information: "[4:27] [Music] [4:29] he [4:34] [Music]" — nothing new lands for over half a minute. 4 · how (the next move)Tighten 4:23-4:59 to a 10-second montage and lay a voiceover naming what the photo shoot is trying to capture over the remaining shots. 5 · rationalePacing is flow of new information, not cut frequency — something should visibly change every ~5 seconds, and silent b-roll here changes nothing. cautionThe 3:55 replay peak sits inside this run, so preserve the specific frames viewers scrubbed back to before trimming the surrounding music.
peak9:00
1 · what the curve showedAudience ticks up to 33.4% for two samples as the sink risk is announced (*+1.9% of audience present, 215 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“oh we're going to sink” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The anticipatory line lands here: "got the cool like cypress trees in the background cloudy Sunshine oh we're going to sink". 4 · how (the next move)Add a riser under 8:39-8:53 starting on "oh we're going to sink" and hold it through the save at 8:54, then drop music on the resolution. 5 · rationaleStarting anticipatory music ~20 seconds before a key moment flattens retention through the buildup — the peak here shows the beat is worth amplifying.
peak9:07
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises to 34.7% for one sample as the near-sink moment resolves (*+4.0% of audience present, 458 viewers regained, 56% vs similar*). 2 · evidence at that second“no sinking today” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind the save itself: "oh we're going to sink so time to put this little bad boy down... no sinking today". 4 · how (the next move)Extend the near-sink beat by 2-3 seconds using bare sound instead of music, then hard-cut into the next segment without the 9:31 reset. 5 · rationaleStretching a conflict beat with music stripped can triple its screen time with stable retention, and this beat is already pulling rewinds.
drop9:15
1 · what the curve showedA seven-second window at 79% through the video loses viewers at 2.37% versus the channel's 0.83% typical here (*27.4x the surrounding stop rate, 1,243 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“I don't have a microphone hooked” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers exit right as a b-roll block ends and the creator restarts with a housekeeping caveat: "I don't have a microphone hooked up to the camera yet". 4 · how (the next move)Cut the mic disclaimer and the "welcome to my new camera section" reset at 9:31-9:44 and hard-join the b-roll directly into the next spoken beat. 5 · rationaleSignaling a new section this late tells viewers the main thing is over — retention drops the moment viewers sense the video is ending.

drop0:09
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 22 seconds shed viewers at the channel's usual intro pace (*11.8% lost, 0.9x the channel's intro average, 4,441 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“welcome back to living in a trailer park” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A channel greeting and premise restatement runs before any hook: "welcome back to living in a trailer park life with her two wheels". 4 · how (the next move)Keep the current open, since it beats the channel's intro average and holds 96.9% at 0:15 (top-third of 299 videos). 5 · rationaleSurgery on an intro that already outperforms the cohort's median and average would risk the +1.4pp lead this video carries at 0:15.
peak6:28
1 · what the curve showedTen seconds earlier the audience rose 3.2% and held for 28 samples across the sponsor-to-auction handoff (*311 viewers regained, 74% vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“head into something super super fun” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The read closes and immediately teases the next segment: "head into something super super fun for the first time my life". 4 · how (the next move)Keep this exact handoff phrasing on future sponsor reads — close the read by naming the next segment's stake, not with a thank-you beat. 5 · rationaleAnticipation-priming into a payoff is what Joos measures as the difference between a 10-20% ad drop and a ~2% one; this transition demonstrably held viewers.
peak6:38
1 · what the curve showedThe audience rose 9.0% and held for 27 samples right as the auction reveal begins (*889 viewers regained, 77% vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“for the first time my life” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The sponsor read ends and the video pivots into the promised premise: "for the first time my life I am learning about the mum Automotive auction". 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 3-5 second tease of this auction reveal into the intro, so first-minute viewers see the hook that later viewers rewind to. 5 · rationale1:00 holds only 56.7%, 4.4pp below the channel median and ranked 84 of 299 — the premise viewers actually rewind for is arriving too late to save early loss.
peak7:50

drop11:04

drop12:25

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:09
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 19 seconds shed a third of the room (*33.4% lost, 2,666 viewers, 2.5x this channel's intro average of 13.4%*). 2 · evidence at that second“8 years ago I learned” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The hook is a personal backstory instead of camera footage: "8 years ago I learned how to ride motorcycles" — exposition before the promised comparison lands. 4 · how (the next move)Recut 0:00-0:15 to open on the side-by-side low-light garage footage referenced at 6:22, then state the comparison in one sentence. 5 · rationaleIntros must deliver the thumbnail promise immediately; the channel's best intro loses 0.0%, so backstory before payoff is the specific lever bleeding this cohort.
peak4:48
1 · what the curve showedThe audio-test setup pulls 165 viewers back and holds for ten samples (*3.4% rose, sits at 43.2%, 63rd percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“GoPro Hero 12 First see how” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The test protocol is spelled out clearly: "GoPro Hero 12 First... then I'm switching over to the DJI" — viewers scrub back to catch the order. 4 · how (the next move)Add an on-screen "Test 1: GoPro / Test 2: DJI" chyron at 4:57 so the sequence is legible without a rewind. 5 · rationaleProgress trackers hold retention; labeling the A/B order removes the confusion driving the rewind and lets the comparison land on first watch.
peak4:58
1 · what the curve showedA second smaller rebound during the same test setup adds 108 viewers over three samples (*2.2% rose, sits at 44.2%, 64th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“switching over to the DJI” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Same test-protocol beat as 4:48: "switching over to the DJI osmo action 4" — viewers confirm which camera they are now hearing. 4 · how (the next move)Merge with the 4:48 chyron fix and add a camera-name lower-third that stays on-screen for the duration of each audio sample. 5 · rationaleTwo rewinds ten seconds apart on the same identification question means the on-screen labeling, not the audio itself, is the friction to remove.
drop6:12
1 · what the curve showedA nine-second stretch drops 488 viewers at 3.6x the channel's norm here (*30.8x the surrounding stop rate, 3.59% versus 1.01% typical*). 2 · evidence at that second“editing Jess here I can't” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)An editor-insert breaks the flow mid-verdict: "editing Jess here I can't believe" interrupts the DJI-preferred conclusion before the low-light evidence arrives. 4 · how (the next move)Cut the meta-aside at 6:08-6:14 and jump straight from the DJI preference statement into the garage low-light footage described at 6:27. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information; a self-referential aside repeats what the viewer already knows and stalls the reveal the segment was building toward.
peak8:04
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs 5.9% and holds for ten samples as the Moto Vlog section starts (*249 viewers regained, sits at 39.3%, 61st percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“up the gain actually to positive” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers rewind to catch the specific gain setting: "up the gain actually to positive 10 or 12" — a concrete number worth copying. 4 · how (the next move)Pin this exact setting as an on-screen card at 8:12 and reference it in the description so first-time viewers do not need to scrub back. 5 · rationaleReplay peaks on measurements and numbers are asset moments; surfacing the number reduces the friction that made viewers rewind in the first place.
drop10:14
1 · what the curve showedNineteen seconds lose 288 viewers at 2.8x the channel's typical stop rate here (*7.0x the surrounding rate, audience falls 38.8% to 35.5%*). 2 · evidence at that second“GoPro has the best internal audio” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The verdict is delivered as a caveat sandwich: "GoPro has the best internal audio quality... it's just not as reliable" — a resolution followed by a walk-back. 4 · how (the next move)Restructure 10:14-10:32 to state the DJI recommendation first, then attach the GoPro-audio caveat as a single clause before moving to battery life. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment tension resolves; resolving the audio question mid-video without immediately raising the next one releases viewers.

The one live-stakes moment on the road is what viewers rewound — give the ride two.

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime15:27 gone by 0:3038% at halfway20% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:08
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 20 seconds sheds nearly a third of the room, running well above the channel's own intro losses (*23.6% lost, 1.7x the channel's intro average, 18,146 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“go watch that entire video over on his channel” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The open recaps the husband's prior video and cross-promotes his channel instead of showing the surprise: "go watch that entire video over on his channel". 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:19-0:27 and open cold on the reveal beat "go ahead and lift it up oh my you crying" before any recap. 5 · rationalePackaging promises a surprise reveal; delivering it inside the first 10 seconds keeps the thumbnail promise and defers the cross-promotion. cautionVerify the cross-promotion isn't a contractual obligation to Jordan Ray's channel; if so, move it to the outro instead of cutting.
peak12:12
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises and holds for 17 samples as the sponsor segue begins (*7.0% rise, 2,076 viewers regained, 73rd percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“I had to get new prescription lenses” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The pivot to sponsor lands on curiosity, not a sales line: "I had to get new prescription lenses because my stigmatism is just getting worse". 4 · how (the next move)Open every future sponsor read on a personal problem sentence like this one, never on "this video is sponsored by". 5 · rationaleReads that open on something the viewer cares about avoid the 10-20% audience cost of a straight ad open.
peak12:22
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises through the sponsor read and holds for 15 samples, well above comparable moments (*7.0% rise sustained, 2,103 viewers regained, 73rd percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“officially time for Mama two wheels” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The read runs while the reveal is teased but not delivered: "it is officially time for Mama two wheels to come see her new beautiful baby". 4 · how (the next move)Keep this ad placement structure on future sponsor reads: tease the reveal, run the read while anticipation is live, then deliver. 5 · rationaleAds hold best at the height of anticipation, not after payoffs; this placement is already the channel's model for future integrations.
peak13:08
1 · what the curve showedAudience climbs sharply as viewers rewind into the reveal moment itself (*6.7% of audience regained, 2,663 viewers, 76th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“baby girl what do you think” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers scrub back to see mom's first reaction: "baby girl what do you think I think she's beautiful you crying". 4 · how (the next move)Build a 20-second riser from 12:55 into 13:08 and hold the reaction shot longer, then tease a second reveal beat (the ride) to keep tension live. 5 · rationaleRewinds mark the emotional peak; extending buildup with anticipatory music holds up to ~10% more of the room into the payoff.
drop13:17
1 · what the curve showedThe reveal window loses 4.2 points of audience where the channel typically GAINS 1.6 points on reveals (*5.3x surrounding stop rate, 10.1x the channel's reveal norm, 3,911 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“let's do the reveal” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The reveal beat is slow and sparse: "let's do the reveal" then long pauses around "I think she's beautiful" with little new visual information landing per second. 4 · how (the next move)Tighten 13:17-14:04 by cutting the dead beats after "she looks gorgeous" and cross-cutting mom's reaction with close-ups of the modified parts every ~5 seconds. 5 · rationalePacing is flow of new information; a reveal that pauses on one emotion for 40 seconds stops progressing and viewers leave the moment tension resolves.
drop14:31
1 · what the curve showedThe outro loses more than a third of remaining viewers where the channel's outros typically lose a tenth (*3.6x the channel's outro average, 9.0x the local norm, 6,285 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“it is now live on his channel” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The video signals it's ending and pivots to plugs: "if you want to see what Jordan did to her motorcycle it is now live on his channel". 4 · how (the next move)Cut 14:34-14:55 and end on "I love you mom so proud of you" within 5 seconds, moving the Jordan plug to a card overlay. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment viewers sense the video is ending; ending on the emotional high and breaking off fast protects the final beat.

drop0:14
1 · what the curve showedThe audience holds at 96.5% at 0:30 then collapses to 57.0% by 1:00, a 39.5-point channel-worst plunge (*+14.6pp above channel median at 0:30, -4.1pp below by 1:00, 8,243 viewers gone*). 2 · evidence at that second“heading up to North Carolina” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The open coasts on packing-up voiceover and a music sting before pivoting, with only 'heading up to North Carolina' as the stated stake. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 0:19-0:40 and reopen on the coldest riding moment from 6:16-6:24, then state the North Carolina parts-install goal in one sentence. 5 · rationalePackaging promises 'unexpected changes' on a solo trip; the current open delivers neither the changes nor the trip, so viewers who stayed for 30s bail once they realise.
drop6:25

Turn the weather complaint into a decision viewers can follow.
peak8:43
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 3.3% and holds for 17 samples as the rider arrives at the Wonderlich US headquarters (*407 viewers regained, audience at 34.9%, 65th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“wonderlick US headquarters” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The destination lands with a concrete name and purpose — 'wonderlick US headquarters' to 'get some new parts put on my dolly girl'. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this arrival cue at 1:00 as the video's stated destination, then tease the specific parts before the ride footage. 5 · rationaleA sustained 17-sample rise on a destination reveal is the video's clearest interest signal; using it as the intro's promise fixes the 0:30-1:00 collapse.
peak8:59

peak10:16
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 2.6% as the new luggage rack goes on, though the lift holds only 1 sample (*345 viewers regained, audience at 36.5%, 76th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“new bar luggage rack” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The moment names the specific upgrade — 'new bar luggage rack' and 'bag protection' — with the installer visibly working. 4 · how (the next move)Show a before/after cut of the rack at 10:16 and hold on the finished bar for 3 seconds before moving to floorboards. 5 · rationaleThe single-sample hold means viewers came for the change and left when narration drifted; a clean visual payoff would extend the peak.
drop10:31

peak4:14

peak4:27

peak4:40

drop7:12

drop12:04

1 · what the curve showedA third of the way in, an eight-fold spike loses viewers well above the channel's rate here and well below peer videos (*7.9x spike, 506 viewers, 34th percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“why is this so much fun” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A ~15 seconds of near-silence sits between 'safely get me to a stopping position' and 'why is this so much fun all right let's try it in sport mode' — dead air before the mode change. 4 · how (the next move)Cut the 6:36-6:51 gap and hard-join 'safely get me to a stopping position' straight into 'all right let's try it in sport mode'. 5 · rationaleSomething should visibly change every ~5 seconds (Joos); a 15-second silent stretch is the valley that invites the exit.
peak12:26
1 · what the curve showedThe earliest of three clustered rises adds 3.8% and holds 40 samples in the 66th percentile (*+3.8%, 286 viewers regained, held 40 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“engine breaking is insane oh my gosh” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The unprompted reaction to regen braking — 'engine breaking is insane oh my gosh' — the moment the bike's defining feature actually lands for the rider. 4 · how (the next move)Move 12:03-12:16 ('holy crap that's amazing... friction on it is so cool') to sit immediately after the first sport-mode acceleration around 6:59. 5 · rationaleEvery cut should raise a question and answer it (Hayden); pairing the acceleration with its visceral reaction closes the loop the current edit leaves open for six minutes. cautionConfirm the 12:03-12:16 audio is not answering an off-camera question that would break continuity if moved; if so, use only the 'engine breaking is insane' line.
peak12:39
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises nearly 5% and holds for 39 samples, sitting in the 67th percentile against similar videos (*+4.9%, 377 viewers regained, held 39 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“sport mode like deceleration was wild” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)This is the post-ride debrief landing the sport-mode payoff — 'sport mode like deceleration was wild that was super fun' — the reaction the ride was building toward. 4 · how (the next move)Tease this exact reaction line in the first 20 seconds with a 'wait for sport mode' cutaway, then let the ride play out to it. 5 · rationaleDopamine spikes at the ANNOUNCEMENT of a reward (Joos); if viewers rewind for this beat, promising it up front pulls the front half through the middle.
peak12:51
1 · what the curve showedA second rise on the same debrief adds 3.7% of the room and holds 37 samples, again above peer videos (*+3.7%, 301 viewers regained, 69th percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“tires are a bit wide” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The honest handling critique — 'the tires are a bit wide so going into a couple of those Corners I was like lean' — a genuine drawback delivered right after praise. 4 · how (the next move)Cut a 6-second 'here's what surprised me' pull-quote from 12:41-12:57 and drop it as the pre-title tease before 0:12. 5 · rationaleA reveal that earns rewinds is an asset (Hayden); mixed verdict from a rider viewers trust is the interest hook the applause open is missing.

drop0:10

Close To Home" opens at 0:00 with 0.0% loss: cold-open on the group ride's most charged moment, then state the safety question. 5 · rationaleThe intro's job is context, stakes and goal fast; restating the thumbnail costs the first 30% of the audience before the video begins.
drop6:30
1 · what the curve showedA small dip on a reflective aside, but the stop rate actually undercuts the channel's norm here (*7.1x the surrounding stop rate, 406 viewers, 0.9x channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“never gonna be a badass biker” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The speaker breaks from the ride story into a self-deprecating tangent: "I'm never gonna be a badass biker it's never gonna happen". 4 · how (the next move)Tighten 6:30-6:54 by cutting the "biker term" digression and rejoining on the TikTok anecdote so the B-story keeps progressing. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information; repeating the same beat about identity stalls the segment while the ride A-story waits.
peak13:40
1 · what the curve showedThe audience scrubs back to the ride payoff, holding the gain for 14 samples (*audience rose 6.7%, 484 viewers regained, 72nd percentile vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“whoa that was awesome” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers return to the wordless riding beat capped by an unguarded reaction: "whoa that was awesome". 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 3-4 second flash of this reaction shot into the 0:00-0:15 cold open so the intro promise matches the moment viewers rewind to. 5 · rationaleA reveal that earns rewinds is an asset; teasing it early gives the opening the emotional peak the current intro lacks.
peak13:50
1 · what the curve showedThe same ride sequence draws a third rewind cluster, confirming this is the video's emotional peak (*audience rose 5.6%, 430 viewers regained, held for 11 samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“we had the road all to ourselves” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewatched beat sits between the reflection "we had the road all to ourselves" and the wordless riding payoff. 4 · how (the next move)Move a 5-second slice of this ride footage into the 2:00 valley as a pattern-interrupt tease, captioned to promise the full ride is coming. 5 · rationalePattern interrupts belong at the graph's valleys, and teasing a proven reward holds viewers through the mid-video stretch that currently sits 15.7pp below channel median.
peak14:00
1 · what the curve showedA second replay lift stacks on the same ride sequence, the video's highest recovery point (*audience rose 5.4%, 438 viewers regained, audience climbs to 22.6%*). 2 · evidence at that second“yes what a great ride” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers linger through the music-only celebration beat: "yes what a great ride" followed by applause. 4 · how (the next move)Extend the music-and-riding beat at 13:53-14:29 by 3-5 seconds and strip narration, letting the applause land before any cut. 5 · rationaleStretching a conflict-resolution beat with music alone can triple screen time with stable retention; this beat is already earning rewinds.
drop15:00
1 · what the curve showedA late spike well above the channel's habit at this position, unusual for this creator (*3.6x the surrounding stop rate, 2.4x channel norm, 379 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“talk about something a little more seriously” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The host verbally signals a tonal shift and a wrap-up frame: "talk about something a little more seriously in this video". 4 · how (the next move)Cut the 14:48-15:04 preamble and open the segment directly on "there are serious serious issues" so viewers hit the substance without a warning. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment viewers sense the video is ending or shifting mode; announcing the pivot cues the exit.

drop0:08

drop2:30

peak4:38

drop5:23

peak7:23

peak10:23

What NOT to do at the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally

published 2023-08-06 · analysed 2026-08-26

1 · Retention breakdown

curve100 samples, stored one per percent runtime16:17 gone by 0:3028.8% at halfway38% still watching methodhazard = (present before − present after) ÷ present before at each moment; baseline = mean hazard of the previous 5 moments, floored; flagged when the excess viewers lost beyond baseline ranks high; a rise is a rewind only when no comparable drop precedes it and the lift survives the next sample

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:10
1 · what the curve showedThe intro sheds a fifth of the audience between 0:10 and 0:29 (*21.9% lost, 8,219 viewers, 1.5x the channel's own intro average*). 2 · evidence at that second“heading to a restaurant that I ate” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The open restates the premise instead of the title's promise: "welcome back to the channel" then a lunch errand — "heading to a restaurant that I ate at last year." 4 · how (the next move)Rebuild the open the way "What Happened To Me?" does it — cold-open on a Sturgis "what NOT to do" moment, then greet. 5 · rationaleThe channel's best intro loses 0% here; delivering the title promise in the first sentence is what closes that 7.7pp gap.
peak3:15
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 1.9% during the GoPro rant (*465 viewers regained, 55% vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“guess whose GoPro stopped working” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)An unscripted grievance breaks the travel-vlog cadence: "guess whose GoPro stopped working… probably gonna make the permanent switch to DJI." 4 · how (the next move)Keep this beat intact and mirror its candid-complaint tone in one more mid-video aside around the bathtub hike. 5 · rationalePattern interrupts hold at valleys; the audience is telling you unscripted opinion outperforms the scripted restaurant recap around it. cautionThe GoPro/DJI mention may be tied to a sponsor or affiliate arrangement — verify before amplifying, and if so, cross-cut the read with the ride.
drop3:54
1 · what the curve showedThe lunch wrap-up bleeds 1,468 viewers across twenty seconds (*12.0x the surrounding stop rate, 2.0x the channel norm here*). 2 · evidence at that second“we are all officially in food Comas” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The segment resolves before the next one starts: "lunch was absolutely amazing we are all officially in food Comas" — tension fully spent with runtime left. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 4:09-4:24 and hard-jump from the sweet-tea beat straight to the bridal veil Falls ride, no "food Comas" bridge. 5 · rationaleRetention drops the moment tension is resolved; killing the post-meal debrief keeps a suspense layer live into the next segment.
peak9:56
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 2.4% for a single sample as the Devil's bathtub attempt is announced (*445 viewers regained, 44% vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“we're gonna try out Devil's bathtub” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The announcement itself is the dopamine hit: "we're gonna try out Devil's bathtub" — a reward being teased, not delivered. 4 · how (the next move)Extend the anticipatory riser from 9:48 through 9:58 and cut the dead music tail so the tease flows straight into the hike footage. 5 · rationaleDopamine spikes at the announcement of a reward; holding the riser through the tease protects the room into the 10:06 drop that currently follows.
drop10:06
1 · what the curve showedA ten-second music-only transition into Devil's bathtub loses 1,697 viewers (*23.2x the surrounding stop rate, 2.1x the channel norm here*). 2 · evidence at that second“we didn't have any luck finding geodes” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Dead air after a failed beat: "we didn't have any luck finding geodes" then music, then a foreign-language caption artifact with no visible progress. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 9:58-10:18 down to a two-second riser and land directly on the 11:40 "welcome to the devil's bathtub" line. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information; twenty seconds of music after admitting failure gives viewers permission to leave before the reveal arrives.
peak11:53
1 · what the curve showedAudience rises 4.0% and holds for five samples as the Devil's bathtub reveal lands (*672 viewers regained, 58% vs similar videos*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's literally a tiny waterfall” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The payoff undercuts itself out loud: "it's literally a tiny waterfall… four feet deep… freezing cold… would not recommend" — the exact "what NOT to do" the title sold. 4 · how (the next move)Tease this line at 0:05 as the cold-open — show the tiny waterfall with the "would not recommend" audio — then structure the video toward it. 5 · rationaleA reveal that earns rewinds is an asset; front-loading the tease keeps the promise the current intro breaks and pulls viewers through the hike.

drop0:11
1 · what the curve showedThe opening 13 seconds lose about one in seven viewers, but that is gentler than the channel usually sees at this position (*3.5x spike, 2,947 viewers, stop rate 7.62% vs the channel's 10.25%*). 2 · evidence at that second“well I guess when it rains it pours” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Rambling setup about the trip timing and destinations rather than a hook: 'well I guess when it rains it pours' followed by dates and rally logistics. 4 · how (the next move)Keep this open; the channel's intros average 13.4% loss and this one lost 11.7%, so preserve the current cold-open cadence rather than recut. 5 · rationaleThe intro already beats the channel's own intro average (0.9x) and holds 295 of 299 peers by 1:00 — surgery risks a proven opening.
peak9:32
1 · what the curve showedViewers scrub back into the coffee-shop arrival and 11% of the room rejoins, held for seven samples (*1,048 viewers regained, audience at 36.2%*). 2 · evidence at that second“okay let's go check it out” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A silent music-only beat over the arrival visual: '[9:30] okay let's go check it out [9:32] [Music]' — a rewatchable establishing moment. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load this arrival shot into the video's cold open as a two-second tease before the trip context lands at 0:11. 5 · rationaleA moment that earns rewinds is an asset; teasing it early gives the opening a proven visual hook without spending new footage.
drop9:45
1 · what the curve showedA twelve-second stretch inside the coffee-shop visit sheds viewers at over sixteen times the surrounding rate (*17.4x spike, 570 viewers, 1.6x the channel norm here*). 2 · evidence at that second“only cost three dollars and six cents” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The narrative pauses on price and menu commentary with no forward motion: 'this large cold brew tastes delicious only cost three dollars and six cents'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 9:50-10:07 down to a single line on the coffee and rejoin on the next travel beat so the shop stop lasts under fifteen seconds. 5 · rationalePacing = flow of new information; the price-and-Danish beat introduces nothing new and stalls the trip narrative the title promised.
peak18:27
1 · what the curve showedA small rebound of 2.0% holds for three samples right at the plug's tail (*146 viewers regained, audience at 25.1%*). 2 · evidence at that second“he's cute he knows it” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A quick reaction cutaway breaks the plug: 'he's cute he knows it it's hot' — a brief pattern interrupt viewers rewind for. 4 · how (the next move)Duplicate this reaction beat as the cold interrupt inside the charity ask, so the plug at 17:59-18:26 carries the same break viewers are already rewinding to. 5 · rationalePattern interrupts belong in the graph's valleys; the audience already told you this cutaway works, so place it where the plug loses them.
drop18:40
1 · what the curve showedA twenty-five second window near the end loses viewers at nearly three times the channel's usual rate for this position (*16.1x spike, 514 viewers, 2.8x channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“donate to charity don't eat for a good cause” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)A charity plug and description CTA land right before the lunch beat: 'head over to the link I'll have it in the description right now and donate to charity'. 4 · how (the next move)Move the forgotten Angels ask to 17:59 while the motorcycle-giveaway tease is still live, and open 18:34 straight on 'alrighty lunchtime'. 5 · rationalePlace asks where suspense is live, never after a payoff — the giveaway tease is the anticipation this plug should ride, not the lunch reveal. cautionVerify the charity plug has no fixed placement commitment; if it does, A/B the reorder against the current cut and keep whichever holds more of the room past 19:04.
peak18:40

It's a good breakfast. It's like dessert for breakfast' — the first character beat between the two hosts. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a similar two-host reaction beat inside the first 45 seconds so new arrivals meet the dynamic before the 0:30 cliff. 5 · rationaleThe rewind sits on personality, not rally footage — evidence the duo interaction is the retention asset, and it's currently buried past the point 58% of viewers already left.
drop3:45

peak8:02

drop8:08

drop0:14

drop7:44
1 · what the curve showedA 15-second beat mid-ride quits at more than double the channel's rate for this position (*16.8x local spike, 2,934 viewers, 2.66% stop vs 1.29% channel norm*). 2 · evidence at that second“nothing to talk about” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rider explicitly narrates dead time: 'about 200 miles since I last turned the camera on because it just looked exactly the same and I had nothing to talk about'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 7:50-8:00 and rejoin on the 'starting to get a little hilly' visual, dropping the self-narrated void entirely. 5 · rationaleJoos: kill all repetition and compress stripping-down phases — a creator announcing nothing happened is the strongest possible bail signal.
peak15:29
1 · what the curve showedThe audience rises sharply as the rider pulls over to gear up against incoming rain (*+7.4% of audience present, 2,551 viewers regained, held 38 samples, 81st percentile vs similar*). 2 · evidence at that second“put my ring gear on” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers scrub back to the decision beat: 'I decided I'm gonna go ahead and pull over here and put my ring gear on'. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load a 3-second tease of this gear-up decision into the cold open to seed the title promise from second one. 5 · rationaleJoos: a reveal that earns rewinds is an asset — tease it early and structure toward it to lift the collapsing 0:30 hold.
peak15:44
1 · what the curve showedA second rise lands on the mileage callout right after gearing up (*+3.8% of audience present, 1,394 viewers regained, held 37 samples, 82nd percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“800 miles in 12 and a half hours” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewind target is the concrete number: 'we have ridden 800 miles in 12 and a half hours'. 4 · how (the next move)Add an on-screen mileage/time counter that ticks across the ride so this number reads as a milestone, not a throwaway line. 5 · rationaleJoos: progress trackers hold retention, and viewers are already rewinding to catch the figure — surface it visually.
peak19:43
1 · what the curve showedA short rise into the hotel arrival where the rain payoff lands (*+3.2% of audience present, 1,301 viewers regained, held 3 samples, 72nd percentile*). 2 · evidence at that second“oh my God I'm so upset” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Viewers replay the emotional break: 'oh my God I'm so upset' right after 'this is not ideal but I'm gonna go find my room'. 4 · how (the next move)Hold this emotional beat 2 seconds longer by stripping music to bare sound before cutting to the 1,000-mile recap. 5 · rationaleJoos: stretching a conflict beat with bare sound can triple screen time at stable retention — this beat is already earning replays.
drop20:28
1 · what the curve showedA 15-second beat inside the rain arrival loses viewers at 11.6x the surrounding rate, though only fractionally above channel norm (*1.25% stop vs 1.11% typical, 1,226 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“audio was so bad” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Audio breaks mid-sentence into a hard cut to a hotel recap: 'well I didn't realize the audio was so bad from recording last night because of how waterlogged my cell phone was'. 4 · how (the next move)Trim 20:29-20:35 and bridge the storm beat directly into the '1,000 miles in 16 hours' payoff without the audio apology. 5 · rationaleJoos: never signal a production seam late in the video — apologizing for audio releases tension the storm sequence just built.

Why we left Ohio.

published 2022-10-19 · analysed 2026-08-26

1 · Retention breakdown

Red marks are flagged drops, green are earned rewinds. Hover a mark for its note.

2 · Each flagged moment: from curve to note

drop0:10
1 · what the curve showedA quarter of the room walks out during the opening twenty seconds (*4.1x spike, 19,756 viewers, audience 97.8%→73.2%*). 2 · evidence at that second“still very dark outside” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The intro is pre-dawn setup narration over dark B-roll — 'it is a little after 7 A.M here in Ohio, it's still very dark outside' — with no stake landed before the music sting. 4 · how (the next move)Rebuild this open the way "What Happened To Me?" does at 0:00, which lost 0.0% — cold-open on 12:32's countdown 'three two one' and applause, then cut back to Ohio. 5 · rationaleIntro lost 25.2% versus a 14.2% channel-kind average; opening on an out-of-context strong-emotion moment is the documented fix for a hockey-stick open.
drop5:47
1 · what the curve showedA music-only montage loses viewers at more than ten times the surrounding rate (*10.8x spike, 2,648 viewers, 54th percentile vs similar*). 2 · evidence at that second“feeling like a roller coaster” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The stretch is a wordless riding montage — captions show only '[Music]' bookending 'feeling like a roller coaster, come and take a ride with me' — no new information for roughly forty seconds. 4 · how (the next move)Trim 5:19-6:16 to a single ten-second cut and overlay a progress cue (miles to Florida, hour of day) so something visibly changes. 5 · rationalePacing is flow of new information, not cuts — a music montage with no progression is the textbook stripping-down phase to compress.
peak11:13
1 · what the curve showedA held six-sample lift sits on the Jess-and-guest banter (*+0.6% present, 151 viewers, 53rd percentile vs similar*). 2 · evidence at that second“nothing but desire actually” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewound line is the flirt-tease exchange — 'what's going on between you and Jess… nothing but desire actually' — a character beat viewers replay. 4 · how (the next move)Move a fifteen-second version of this exchange into the 2:00 sag where the channel already trails median by 7.4pp. 5 · rationalePeak-end structuring says force an emotional peak mid-video; a proven replay beat is the strongest candidate to lift the 41.0% floor at 2:00. cautionThe banter may rely on the earlier setup of who the guest is — if so, add a one-line name card when relocating.
peak11:43
1 · what the curve showedA smaller rewatch clusters on the giveaway call-out (*+0.9% present, 249 viewers, held two samples*). 2 · evidence at that second“now's the chance because you could win” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Jess names the raffle mechanic — 'if you're gonna buy a raffle ticket now now's the chance because you could win' — and viewers scrub back for the terms. 4 · how (the next move)Burn the raffle deadline and entry link on-screen for the full 11:52-12:11 window so viewers get the detail without rewinding. 5 · rationaleA rewind driven by missed information is a legibility fix, not a content asset — surfacing the detail converts scrubs into forward watching.
peak12:42
1 · what the curve showedThe audience rewinds into the countdown-to-face-reveal beat (*+1.9% present, 519 viewers regained, audience 25.8%*). 2 · evidence at that second“it's all been for this” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)This is the payoff to the video's central tease — 'why don't you show your face… it's all been for this' — landing right after the 'three two one' countdown. 4 · how (the next move)Tease this reveal inside the first minute with the countdown audio and a blurred frame, then withhold the face until 12:42 as now. 5 · rationaleDopamine spikes at the announcement of a reward — front-loading the tease exploits the one moment viewers already rewind to.
drop14:41
1 · what the curve showedThe sign-off triggers a cliff thirty seconds before the video ends (*6.0x spike, 6.5x channel norm, 3,068 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“we're gonna get back to bike night” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)Jess audibly signals the outro — 'thanks Jess block that's it we're gonna get back to bike night' — releasing viewers before the 15:01 beat lands. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 14:27-14:52 and hand straight from the face-reveal beat into the 15:01 'I'm sorry' moment, killing the goodbye entirely. 5 · rationaleRetention collapses the instant viewers sense an ending; this spike runs 6.5x the channel's own norm for this position, so the wrap-up itself is the cost. cautionThe subscribe-to-his-channel plug may be a promised cross-promo — if so, move that single sentence into the description and keep the cut.

drop0:09

[Applause] ... [Music]” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The open is a wordless music-and-applause montage with no context or stakes — the transcript carries only '[Music]', 'thank you', '[Applause]' before 0:30. 4 · how (the next move)Trial a 15-second cold open modeled on 'What Happened To Me?' — lead with a spoken stakes line over the loudest rally footage before any music bed. 5 · rationaleThe intro's job is context plus stakes plus goal delivered fast; a silent montage delivers none and the channel's best intro at 0:00 loses 0.0%.
peak3:33
1 · what the curve showedViewers rewind into the campsite arrival and the audience holds elevated for five samples, the longest sustained lift in the video (*+2.4% of the audience present, 1,017 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“back in this adorable little Nook campsite” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewind sits on a visual reveal of the sleeping setup: 'back in this adorable little Nook campsite ... some people say it's Overkill but I'm gonna sleep very comfortably'. 4 · how (the next move)Show the finished campsite setup as a 3-second cutaway inside the 0:30 intro to preview the payoff viewers are already returning to. 5 · rationaleWithholding the finished thing and teasing it early trains viewers to wait for the reveal instead of leaving in the first 30 seconds.
drop7:16
1 · what the curve showedA 28-second stretch mid-video quits at 2.7x the channel's norm here, unusual for this creator at the halfway mark (*13.6x the surrounding stop rate, 4,034 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“we did so good we were at a dead end” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rider arrives breathless and recaps a moment viewers did not see: 'we did so good we were at a dead end for a hot second' — verbal recap with no new visual information. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 7:31-7:44 and rejoin on 'we're going to the river man' over the first river-bound riding shot. 5 · rationalePacing is the flow of new information; a spoken recap of an off-screen moment adds none and viewers leave the instant progression stalls.
peak7:16
1 · what the curve showedThe dead-end arrival draws a one-sample rewind even as the same moment bleeds viewers forward (*+2.4% of the audience present, 910 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“we did so good we were at a dead end” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewind lands on the emotional beat 'we did so good we were at a dead end for a hot second' — viewers want the story of the dead end they never saw. 4 · how (the next move)Replace the recap with a 10-second cutaway of the actual dead-end moment, cross-cut with the arrival celebration. 5 · rationaleThe rewind proves demand for the dead-end story; showing it visually converts the same beat from a drop into a held peak. cautionVerify footage of the dead-end exists in the raw rushes; if it does not, trial a still-frame map cutaway instead.
peak11:27
1 · what the curve showedViewers scrub back to the morning-of-departure beat and the audience rises, holding for two samples (*+4.1% of the audience present, 1,265 viewers regained*). 2 · evidence at that second“see how many miles we're at” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The rewind lands on the setup for the odometer reveal — 'let's go hop on the bike and see how many miles we're at' — a number viewers want to hear again. 4 · how (the next move)Front-load the odometer count as a title-card teaser in the first 30 seconds so the number viewers rewind for is promised up top. 5 · rationaleA reveal that earns rewinds is an asset; teasing it early pulls the whole video toward the moment already proven to hold.
drop11:36
1 · what the curve showedA 19-second beat at the three-quarter mark quits at 3.3x this channel's norm, atypical for the creator this late (*12.2x the surrounding stop rate, 2,330 viewers*). 2 · evidence at that second“it is 7 30 in the morning and the sun just came out” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The host stops to narrate the time and location before the next leg: 'it is 7 30 in the morning and the sun just came out ... time for me to hit the road'. 4 · how (the next move)Cut 11:32-11:55 and jump from the morning shot straight to 'current odometer says 32 086 miles' over the odometer close-up. 5 · rationaleSomething should visibly change every ~5 seconds; a spoken time-check with no new stake stalls progression right where the odometer reveal is the actual hook.

peak14:37

peak24:58

drop0:12
1 · what the curve showedThe sponsor pivot from the event tease into an Omaze read sheds roughly a fifth of the room across 24 seconds (*4.9x spike, 8,640 viewers, 97.8% to 75.0%*). 2 · evidence at that second“thanks to today's sponsor omaze” (transcript) 3 · why (the check or the quote)The intro turns from the event promise straight into a giveaway plug, quoting "thanks to today's sponsor omaze" before any payoff lands. 4 · how (the next move)Trial cutting the Omaze read into the ride footage after 5:56 while suspense is live, opening the read on the Buick GNX itself rather than "sponsor." 5 · rationaleThis intro already beats the channel's own intro average (*10.7% vs 14.2%, 0.8x*), so the opening is not the defect — the ad placement inside it is. cautionOmaze contract may lock the sponsor slot to the opening; if so, keep placement and rewrite the first sentence around the GNX prize.
peak5:56

drop15:39

drop0:06

peak7:58

drop8:06

drop9:53
